text:
maya: Heads up — thinking about tenant boundary for authz routing. Our current gateway pins requests to org-model mapping, but we’re seeing quota double-counting when calls are proxied with cross-project service accounts. Anyone seen this lately?

alex: Is this the case where client calls with sa:projects/123/serviceAccounts/ingest@..., gateway attrs authn.project=123 authn.org=456, and then we both route and increment quota in two places? Can you paste a short example?

maya: Exactly. Minimal repro: client uses impersonated SA from project 123, request header X-Forwarded-For from tenant 456. Metering shows tokens++ for project 123 and org 456 separately. Logs: `authz: billing_project=123, audit_org=456`. We end up billing/alerting twice.

sam: We have a stale doc (linked in #internal) that describes claim precedence. Decision point: do we use credential-origin (SA project) or request-origin (calling project) for quota attribution?

henri: From an audit perspective credential-origin is safer. From billing perspective request-origin often makes more sense. Could we emit both and pick one as canonical?

maya: Proposal: add an `attribution_policy` in routing config with values `credential | request | hybrid`. Hybrid emits both labels but only one is used for quota increments. Gateway would add headers: `X-Attribution-Billing` and `X-Attribution-Audit`. Example patch: ```http
X-Attribution-Billing: project:123
X-Attribution-Audit: org:456
```

alex: Dashboards/alerts will break if we start emitting both without a clear canonical field. Suggest we standardize on `canonical_attribution` + `aux_attribution` headers so telemetry consumers have a single source for quota logic.

devex-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout created for eng-platform/routing-attrib v2 — canary=5% in us-east-1.

sam: For quotas, we MUST avoid double increments. If hybrid, metering should increment only the canonical attribution. Aux should be attached to logs/metrics as labels for debugging.

maya: Agreed. Also need Console UX — customers should be able to see "Attributed vs Billed" breakdown. I'll sketch a widget that shows both and highlights canonical.

henri: Security note: impersonation flows must retain originating caller in the audit trail. Add claim `originating_project` to tokens we mint for impersonation so audit consumers can reconstruct the causal chain.

alex: Implementation notes: gateway change + telemetry schema v3. Metering job must read `X-Attribution-Billing` fallback to token.claims.billing_project if header missing. I'll add a feature flag `attrib_v2` to gate behavior.

maya: Who wants gateway PR + tests? @alex can you own gateway headers? @sam can own metering/dashboards?

alex: I’ll take the gateway PR. Add headers, flag, and unit tests. ETA: PR by next Tue.

sam: I’ll update metering and dashboards. Will add integration test that verifies single increment for canonical and labels aux attribution. ETA next Wed. Will also prep eng-releases rollout doc.

maya: :thumbsup: I’ll update the internal doc and Console mockups. Also will add a short migration guide for customers that rely on current attribution behavior.

henri: :thinking_face: One more question — if billing_to=credential, some orgs expect org-level discounts. We should loop in Billing to confirm policy and any overrides.

alex: Good point — pinging billing. I’ll open a Jira and link it here.

devex-bot: deploy-bot: canary scheduled for 2026-04-01 04:00 UTC (eng-platform routing-attrib v2, 5%).

maya: Thanks all — we’ll sync in the weekly infra sync to lock the policy if PRs look good.
